messages:
maya: FYI I pulled a few perf traces from last night's canary. Seeing a regression in A10 p95 for continuous batching when short + long requests interleave. p95 up ~18% vs baseline.

maya: Repro steps: steady background mixed-length traffic (avg 120 tokens) + occasional 8k-token streams. Regression shows up after ~30m.

maya: Attaching the short profiler dump (trimmed):
```
kernel_select: 0.52s
kv_copy: 0.18s
attention_fwd: 0.34s
attention_bwd: 0.00s
beam_pack: 0.06s
allreduce: 0.00s
cpu_prep: 0.12s
queue_wait: 0.27s (spikes)
```
more:
julien: @maya thanks. queue_wait spikes + kv_copy look suspicious. Could be KV cache thrash when long sequences cause fragmentation and different kernel path chosen.

julien: Two quick hypotheses: 1) max_tokens_per_batch too high for A10 so kernel selector flips to large-seq kernel causing memory blowouts and async copies. 2) queue policy packs short+long leading to inefficient padding and KV eviction churn.

sam: I ran a baseline micro-run earlier on T4/A10/L4 with the new kernel selector flags. Observed kernel-fit signal toggling at ~32k tokens which aligns with your timing.

sam: Raw numbers (p95 generation latency, 1h mixed trace):
- T4: baseline 210ms -> regression 245ms
- A10: baseline 130ms -> regression 155ms
- L4: baseline 190ms -> regression 205ms
- A100: baseline 95ms -> no regression
- H100: baseline 82ms -> no regression

rachel: Interesting that A100/H100 unaffected — matches kernel selection threshold idea (they use fp16 kernels that handle KV packing better).

maya: Proposed short-term mitigations: reduce max_tokens_per_batch and add a spillover window to avoid packing very long sequences with short ones. Also try forcing kernel_selector to prefer small-seq kernel for A10 until we patch KV path.

julien: Agreed. I pushed a quick config patch to canary that does:
```yaml
continuous_batching:
  max_batch_items_by_gpu:
    L4: 28
    T4: 32
    A10: 40
    A100: 96
    H100: 128
  max_tokens_per_batch_by_gpu:
    L4: "12000"
    T4: "16000"
    A10: "24000"
    A100: "64000"
    H100: "96000"
  pack_policy: "size_buckets" # avoid mixing <1k and >4k
  spillover_window_ms: 45
```
Note: numbers are conservative for now.

perf-bot: nightly-bench #176777: canary applied config patch at 2026-03-18T01:42:00Z, running 3h mixed workload.

maya: After patch (first 90m) A10 p95 dropped back to +3% vs baseline, queue_wait spikes reduced. T4 also improved slightly. No observable regressions on A100/H100.

sam: I also instrumented KV eviction counters — eviction_rate fell by ~72% after the spillover + bucket pack policy on A10. That matches hypothesis.

rachel: Good. For next steps we should: 1) run extended 24h canary to ensure steady-state, 2) add finer telemetry in kernel_selector to record why a kernel was chosen (seq_len histogram), 3) schedule a kernel-fix sprint for kv_copy path.

julien: I'll open an RFC with kernel selector telemetry and proposed patch for KV copy async batching. Also will add a flag to prefer small-seq kernels below threshold so we can rollout safely.

maya: Action items:
- julien: RFC + small-seq preference flag (ETA 2d)
- sam: start 24h canary with current config (ETA run start in 30m)
- rachel: add dashboard cards for eviction_rate, kernel_choice_hist, queue_wait_p95 (ETA end of day)

maya: Thanks all. If 24h canary looks good we'll promote config to staging and run perf regression suite against L4/A10/T4. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: canary-complete: 24h run scheduled -> queued (will post results).
